name: Sterling-Nakamura Biometric Spoof Kit BSK-2
description: A compact kit containing tools for replicating and spoofing biometric authentication systems — fingerprint molds, retinal pattern contact lenses, voice modulation software, and gait adjustment insoles. The BSK-2 starts with a target's biometric data (obtained through surveillance, data breach, or physical collection) and produces physical devices that replicate those biometrics well enough to defeat standard commercial scanners. The fingerprint molds use silicone casting from lifted prints, the retinal lenses project a stored pattern over the wearer's own retina, and the voice software processes the user's speech in real-time to match the target's vocal characteristics.

specifications.gait: Insoles that alter stride pattern and cadence
specifications.limitations: Does not defeat live tissue verification

story_hooks: A secured facility was accessed using perfect biometric replicas of an authorized employee — the employee was at home at the time, and the BSK-2 components found at the scene show the biometrics were captured from public surveillance footage.

A BSK-2 has been used to frame a specific individual for multiple crimes — their biometric signatures appear at crime scenes they never visited, and the evidence is convincing enough for arrest warrants.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modular case resembling a high-end cosmetics or jewelry organizer—flat, rectangular, with multiple shallow compartments and precision-fitted foam inserts. Designed for discretion and portability rather than intimidation. Interior reveals organized trays of silicone molds, contact lens vials, electronic insoles, and a slim laptop-sized voice processing unit.
physical_description.dimensions: 35 cm × 22 cm × 8 cm (briefcase-sized, fits under a coat or in a messenger bag)
physical_description.weight_description: 500 grams total—easily carried one-handed, pocketable components include the retinal lenses and voice processor dongle
physical_description.primary_material: Matte gunmetal aluminum frame with reinforced polymer composite trays; silicone and medical-grade resin for molds
physical_description.finish: Brushed titanium-gray exterior with soft-touch rubber grip corners; interior compartments lined with anti-static foam and fabric dividers
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray and matte black with accent neon-blue indicator lights on the voice processor module; vials of molds display translucent flesh-tone silicone
physical_description.interface_elements: Small 4-inch touchscreen on the integrated voice processor unit (displays waveform analysis and confidence percentages); USB-C charging port; labeled foam compartments with microdose syringes for silicone application; contact lens storage pods with biometric registry holograms
distinctive_features: Magnetic clasp system that doubles as a Faraday pocket for blocking scanner interference
Holographic 'biometric template' micro-displays embedded in the contact lens storage pods—flickering retinal patterns visible at angles
Texture-matched insole compartment with pressure-mapping grid visible through clear acrylic
Integrated cooling gel pack slot (keeps molds fresh mid-operation)
Nested tool organizer with precision tweezers, applicators, and a micro-3D scanner for print verification
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura logo (interlocking S-N cipher in chrome) on clasp; discrete regulatory stamp reading 'GLMZ TIER 3+ LICENSED SECURITY EQUIPMENT' on rear; serial number etched in silver
physical_description.condition_typical: In active use: case open with one or two compartments accessed, contact lens case beside a small mirror, voice processor screen glowing with real-time audio analysis, insoles positioned on a workbench or the user's feet
